title: add benchmark-lab profiling baselines and reporting pipeline v39
author: Nina Patel
description:
Motivation: consolidate profiling baselines, add representative workload runners for mixed and inference-heavy traffic, and wire up the reporting pipeline (v39) so nightly runs produce standardized artifacts for the dashboard and perf-alerting. Changes are additive and intended to make regression detection faster and reduce noise from skewed sampling.

Summary of changes: added new profiling baseline configs for mixed/qa/throughput suites, introduced a 'mixed-representative' runner that simulates multi-tenant traffic patterns, upgraded the reporting pipeline to include token-level latency histograms and KV-cache hit-rate metrics, and added ingestion hooks for the perf-dashboard. Includes small docs and a canary job in CI for nightly runs.

Checklist: - [x] Add profiling baseline configs and runner harnesses - [x] Wire reporting pipeline (S3 -> processing -> BigQuery/warehouse ingest) - [x] Add CI nightly workflow + canary job - [x] Update perf dashboard ingestion schema and docs - [x] Add eval hooks to compare new runs vs. baseline

Testing & validation: local run + canary in test infra produced stable baselines for 6 representative models (gpt-medium, redwood-7b, redwood-7b-q4, opt-6.7b, llm-lite) and three workload mixes. End-to-end CI nightly job run succeeded after two reruns (one transient networking timeout). Reporting artifacts include: summary csv, token_latency_histogram.json, kv_cache_hit_rates.csv.

Notes: This is the next iteration (v39) of ongoing benchmark-lab improvements; aims to reduce noise in daily alerts by surfacing histogram-based regressions. Follow-ups: small optimization to runner pacing logic (ENG-6103) and adding an SLO-driven alerting rule (ENG-5421).
